lessons.title: Checking on Our Spring Seeds
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe how their planted seed has grown since Week 26.
lessons.main_activity: Children observe and measure their planted seedlings using cubes, comparing to their earlier prediction.
resources_needed: Planted pots from Week 26, linking cubes

differentiation.extension: Compare measurement to prediction and explain difference

lessons.assessment_notes: Note observational and measurement skill over time — evidence for UTW.3/MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Share growth results as a class.
lessons.home_link: Check on any plants growing at home.

lessons.title: Story Time: 'The Enormous Turnip'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retell why teamwork was needed in the story.
lessons.main_activity: Read the story, discussing why everyone needed to work together to pull up the turnip.
key_questions: Why couldn't one person pull it alone?
What happened when everyone worked together?

differentiation.extension: Explain the teamwork message in detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension and understanding of cooperation — evidence for LIT.1/PSED.3.
lessons.plenary: Discuss a time you worked as a team.
lessons.home_link: Talk about working together on a task at home.

lessons.title: Counting Characters Pulling the Turnip
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count the characters joining the line, adding one at a time.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap one more from earlier in the year.
lessons.main_activity: Using character counters/pictures, children recreate the story's growing line, counting how many are pulling after each new character joins.
key_questions: How many after one more joins?

differentiation.extension: Count up to 6+ and explain the growing total

lessons.assessment_notes: Note counting and one-more understanding in context — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of the growing line count.
lessons.home_link: Practise counting 'one more' with toys at home.

lessons.title: Vegetables That Grow Underground
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name a vegetable that grows underground.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the enormous turnip growing underground.
lessons.main_activity: Discuss other vegetables that grow underground (carrot, potato, onion) vs above ground, sorting picture cards.
key_questions: Does this vegetable grow underground or above ground?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of plant growth locations — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Look at vegetables at home and guess where they grew.

lessons.title: Writing About Our Plant's Growth
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to attempt to write a sentence about their plant's growth.
lessons.main_activity: Children draw their plant and attempt to write a simple sentence (e.g. 'my plant is tall') using known phonics sounds.

differentiation.extension: Independent phonetic attempt at a short sentence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note writing progress and purposeful recording — evidence for LIT.3.
lessons.plenary: Share plant growth writing with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Write about a plant's growth together if growing something at home.

lessons.title: Measuring and Comparing Plant Heights
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare the heights of different plants using non-standard units.
lessons.main_activity: Children compare their plant's height to a partner's using linking cubes, discussing whose is taller/shorter.
key_questions: How many cubes tall is yours?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note comparative measurement skill — evidence for MATHS.2.
lessons.home_link: Compare heights of plants or objects at home.

lessons.title: What Do Plants Need? Full Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explain all the things a plant needs to grow well.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap what plants need from Week 5 and Week 26.
lessons.main_activity: Conduct a simple comparison: one plant with water/light, one without, discussing predictions and revisiting results later in the week.
key_questions: What do you think will happen to the plant without light/water?
Why do plants need these things?

differentiation.extension: Predict and explain the experiment's likely outcome

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of plant needs and scientific prediction — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Recap the experiment set up today.
lessons.home_link: Talk about what happens if a plant doesn't get water.

lessons.title: Retelling 'The Enormous Turnip'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retell the story's key events in sequence.
lessons.main_activity: Using picture cards, children retell the story sequence using sequencing words and props.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note sequencing and retelling ability — evidence for LIT.1/CL.2.
lessons.plenary: One group retells to the class.
lessons.home_link: Retell the story to someone at home.

lessons.title: Sharing Vegetables Fairly
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to share a group of vegetable counters equally between people.
lessons.main_activity: Children practise sharing vegetable counters equally between 2-3 puppets, checking fairness.
key_questions: Is that fair? How do you know?
What if there's one left over?

differentiation.extension: Share 6-9 objects between 2-3 people, discuss remainders

lessons.assessment_notes: Note early division/sharing understanding — evidence for MATHS.2.
lessons.home_link: Practise sharing vegetables or snacks fairly at home.

lessons.title: Checking the Plant Experiment
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to observe and explain the results of the plant needs experiment.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the experiment set up on Wednesday.
lessons.main_activity: Children observe and compare the two plants (with/without water and light), discussing the results and why they happened.

differentiation.support: Describe what they see with adult support
differentiation.extension: Explain the reasons for the difference independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note ability to draw conclusions from a simple experiment — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Class conclusion about what plants need to stay healthy.
lessons.home_link: Look after a plant carefully at home, giving it what it needs.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Plant Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read simple plant-themed words.
lessons.main_activity: Phonics stations reading plant-themed word cards and simple sentences (e.g. 'dig a big pot').

differentiation.support: Read simple CVC words with support

lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application to themed vocabulary — evidence for LIT.2.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading plant words over the week.

lessons.title: Patterns in a Vegetable Patch
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to continue a repeating pattern using vegetable counters.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a simple ABAB vegetable pattern.
lessons.main_activity: Children continue and create their own repeating pattern using vegetable counters/stickers in a 'vegetable patch' row.
key_questions: What comes next in this pattern?
Can you make your own pattern?

differentiation.support: Continue simple ABAB pattern with support

lessons.assessment_notes: Note pattern recognition and creation — evidence for MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Display and admire patterned vegetable patch rows.
lessons.home_link: Look for and create patterns with vegetables or toys at home.

lessons.title: Growing Plants Recap Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about growing plants learned this week.
lessons.main_activity: Contribute to a class 'Growing Plants' display summarising plant needs, underground vegetables, and the experiment results.
key_questions: What have we learned about growing plants?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about growing plants with your family.

lessons.title: Growing Plants Quiz Game
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer recall questions about plants learned this week.
lessons.main_activity: Quiz-style game asking questions about plant needs, vegetables, and the experiment from the week.
key_questions: What does a plant need to grow?
lessons.assessment_notes: Assess recall and comprehension — evidence for LIT.1/CL.1.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on plant facts learned this week.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Counting, Measuring, Sharing
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply counting, measuring, and sharing skills learned this week.
lessons.main_activity: Rotate through 3 stations: counting characters/one more, measuring plant heights, sharing vegetables fairly.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising measuring and sharing over the weekend.
